context: Exploratory refinement after v1 was refuted by a t=1 cherry. This is not a fresh held-out certification.
statement: For all ordinary rooted binary trees T,U on X and every cherry {a,b} in T, if the directed U-path embedding between a and b has at least two outgoing off-path child edges, then there exists a minimum agreement forest with singleton {a} or singleton {b}.
t_definition: Count U edges (parent,child) whose parent belongs to the minimal vertex embedding U[{a,b}] and whose child does not belong to it.
failure_criterion: A pair and cherry with t>=2 such that every minimum agreement forest contains neither endpoint singleton.
search: Replay the saved exact n=3,4,5 corpus; preserve every first counterexample per t value.
acceptance: An exact counterexample can refute the statement after independent replay; finite survival does not prove it.
